blocks.text: Setting up Gmail for onboarding workflows on Mac

Since there is no official Gmail app for Mac, you should create a web app to keep your inbox separate from your general browsing. In Chrome, navigate to your inbox, click the three-dot menu, select Save and Share, then Install page as app. For Safari users on macOS Sonoma or later, open your inbox, click File, then Add to Dock. This gives you a standalone icon in your Dock and allows you to use ⌘ + Tab to switch between your email and your CRM or project management tools.
Using keyboard shortcuts to manage email volume

Onboarding specialists handle a high volume of messages. Mouse usage slows you down. Enable shortcuts by clicking the gear icon, selecting See all settings, then choosing the General tab. Scroll down to Keyboard shortcuts and select Keyboard shortcuts on. Once active, press ? to see the full list of commands. Use c to compose, e to archive, r to reply, and a to reply all. These shortcuts allow you to process your inbox without leaving your keyboard.

Lazur helps you manage your email workflow by acting as a voice assistant that understands your screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about settings or navigation. Use the fn key to dictate long onboarding emails directly into the compose window.

If you are sending many personalized onboarding emails, be aware of Google sending limits. Workspace accounts allow up to 2,000 recipients per day. Personal accounts are limited to 500. Exceeding these limits can result in a 24-hour block on your account. Track your outreach carefully to ensure you do not trigger this restriction during peak onboarding periods.

blocks.text: Create labels for each stage of the onboarding process, such as Pre-kickoff, Active, and Pending Signature. Use filters to automatically move emails from specific domains into these labels. This keeps your primary inbox clear. You can find these settings under the Labels and Filters and Blocked Addresses tabs in your Gmail settings menu.

If you see a 502 error or a general connection issue, clear your browser cache and cookies. Conflicts with browser extensions can also cause issues. Try opening Gmail in an Incognito window to see if the problem persists. If it works there, disable your extensions one by one to find the culprit.

If you prefer a native Mac experience, tools like Mimestream or Apple Mail connect to Gmail via OAuth. These clients provide features like unified inboxes and better integration with macOS system notifications. Always verify that your chosen client supports OAuth, as Google no longer supports less secure apps that only use a username and password.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide an official native desktop app for macOS. You can create a web app using Chrome or Safari to get a similar experience.

faq.question: How do I enable keyboard shortcuts in Gmail?
faq.answer: Go to Settings, select See all settings, then under the General tab, toggle Keyboard shortcuts to on.

faq.question: What is the daily sending limit for Gmail?
faq.answer: Google Workspace accounts can send to 2,000 recipients per day, while personal Gmail accounts are limited to 500.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me with my Gmail workflow?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use Lazur to dictate emails, find specific settings, or ask for guidance on how to navigate the Gmail interface using your voice.
